data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced an overall deterioration of GBP 4.1 million on prior years' provisions in 2018. This was driven by strengthenings in Third Party Liability, Marine, Aviation and Transport, and Fire and Other Damage to Property, partially offset by releases in Energy and Reinsurance Acceptances. Specific events impacting prior years included a fire on a yacht in Germany and various large casualty claims for the 2016 year of account, as well as 2017 catastrophe losses (Hurricanes Maria, Irma, Harvey) and non-catastrophe losses (Maersk Honam fire, Oakland property fire, casualty consortium losses) impacting the 2017 year of account. Favourable development was noted for 2015 and prior years, including releases related to the World Trade Centre litigation.
raw_causal_phrases: An overall deterioration of GBP 4.1 million on prior years' provisions was experienced during the year.

Deteriorations of GBP 2.0 million on third party liability, GBP 2.8 million on marine, aviation and transport and GBP 3.4 million on fire and other damage to property were partially offset by improvements of GBP 2.2 million on energy and GBP 1.8 million on reinsurance acceptances.
Reserves in respect of the 2015 and prior years of account continue to develop satisfactorily, generating a surplus of GBP 0.7 million during the 2018 calendar year.

Following the ruling in favour of insurers in respect of the last remaining dispute in a sprawling litigation over liability from the deadly attacks on the World Trade Centre in September 2001, further releases have been made from the reserves held to cover this event.
during late September 2018 the back years were impacted by a fire on a yacht nearing completion in the Lurssen shipyard in Germany.

The 2017 year witnessed a significant increase in losses from a catastrophe perspective, with the syndicate's largest natural catastrophe loss arising from Hurricane Maria closely followed by Hurricane Irma and Hurricane Harvey.
The 2018 losses from the California wildfires, the Hawaiian volcanic eruptions, Hurricane Michael and, to a lesser extent, Hurricane Florence, have also impacted the 2017 year of account.

The largest non-catastrophe losses impacting the 2017 account were a fire in the cargo hold of the Maersk Honam in the marine account, a major fire in a property under construction in Oakland and losses emanating from the main market casualty consortium.
